name: Cement mortar for ductile iron pipe
description:
This unit process reflects cement mortar manufacturing. The inventory for this process only includes material inputs necessary for mortar production. The process excludes energy use associated with onsite mixing of mortar.

The process is normalized to the functional unit of  1 kg mortar production.
category: 31-33: Manufacturing/3273: Cement and Concrete Product Manufacturing

processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: Inventory exchange values were sourced directly from the cited EPA report on disinfection options in municipal drinking water treatment. Background data sources have, in some cases, been updated to reflect newer and/or public data sources. Elementary flows were mapped to the federal elementary flow list.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Excludes energy associated with mixing the mortar.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Inventory adapted from literature. See sources.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Cement mortar process is standardized per kg of mortar produced.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: Scope: material inputs. Data was adapted from literature. Some relevant flows not captured.Uncertainty ranges are not available for this data.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This is a proxy process that consists only of basic material inputs necessary to make cement mortar. If this input is a significant contributor to impact in your product system, a sensitivity assessment or another source of data is recommended.

sources.name: Xue et al (2019) LCA of Urban Water Systems

reviews.details:
Proof reading details: Passed
Other details: none

processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
This process is intended to be used as a background process by LCA practitioners, industry and the general public.

Situation C2 - Accounting, without system-external interatctions. The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system excluding existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model.
